807	  **The transformer did not change.** The three mechanisms each landed on one
808	  seam, and the seams are the device counterparts of the three `ForwardEmbeds`
809	  grew in Q8.2: `Embeddings`+`UploadEmbeds` (the scatter is a host edit of
810	  the lookup, because the ids do not determine the rows), `SetRoPE` (the
811	  mrope table is uploaded rather than built as 0..T-1), and
812	  `RunHooked`+`AddRows` (the deepstack features are added at the pad slots
813	  between layers — one dispatch per image per layer, on `dit_gate_add` with
814	  its gate switched off, staged through the attention branch's own dead
815	  output tensor). `upload` is now `Embeddings` followed by `UploadEmbeds` and
816	  the plain table, so the t2i path runs the same code: `TestGPUEncoder`
817	  re-measures Q1's en/cjk/empty at **0.024 / 0.027 / 0.21, unchanged**.
818	  **Gates**, against `out/qi21vision` with the dump's *own* tower rows as the
819	  conditions (which makes it a gate on the text encoding rather than on the
820	  pair, exactly as Q8.2's two-image case argued): **one image 0.059, two
821	  images 0.064**, the pad mask exact, and layer 0 at **1.1e-3** against a
822	  4x bound — the shallow reading is what keeps a mistake in the three new
823	  mechanisms from hiding under the fp16 one. Controls: plain RoPE instead of
824	  mrope **133x** the bound, no deepstack injection **61x**, the conditions
825	  swapped refused at the row count. Two runs identical.
826	  **The bound is measured and it is 2.4x the t2i path's, and that is not a
827	  bug**: `TestGPUEditLadder` (the permanent instrument, `QI21_LADDER=1`,
828	  ~50 GB) walks the same run against the CPU port layer by layer and finds
829	  **Q1's mechanism unchanged and in the same place** — flat at ~1.1e-3 through
830	  layers 0-5, the massive-activation channel appearing at layer 6 (rms
831	  0.98 → 21.1) carrying an absolute error of 4.46 *flat*, a second jump at
832	  layer 16 whose 8.83 stays 8.83 **in the same column for 18 layers**, and
833	  then the cancellation in layers 34-35 surfacing it: 0.0049 → 0.0146 →
834	  0.0532. The last two layers are the whole of the deviation. And the
835	  *absolute* error does not move between the two paths at all — the worst
836	  element is **2.38 for the t2i prompt and for both edit prompts**, measured
837	  in the same hour; what the 2.4x buys is a different worst relative element
838	  under a lower rms floor. The official bf16 pipeline is rel 2.0 on this
839	  checkpoint, 30x further out.
840	
841	  **Q8.5 — the DiT's edit path on the GPU. Done 2026-09-20**
842	  (`qimage/dit/gpu.go`, ~120 lines changed; `dit_kvcache.comp` and a rewrite
843	  of `dit_attn_causal.comp` are the shader work). **An edit's transformer at
844	  the served shape — a 1024² target on one 1024² reference — is prefill
845	  5.47/5.52 s and cached steps 2.70/2.71 s, so 40 steps is 110.7/111.3 s**
846	  against a generation's 90.7. That is the "slightly more expensive than a
847	  generation" this file predicted, now measured: +22%, all of it the prefix
848	  in every step's attention.
849	  Four things had to change, and three of them are about the prefix being
850	  thousands of rows instead of forty:
851	  - **The condition latents go through `img_in`.** They are latents in the
852	    same sequence, so they take the target's own projection — one GEMM per
853	    condition block off the same narrowed `aLat`, issued in ascending row
854	    order because a GEMM writes whole 128-row tiles and overruns a short
855	    block. The projected *text* rows then land by copy dispatch rather than
856	    by host write, since a host write cannot be ordered after a dispatch
857	    that has not been submitted.
858	  - **The block-causal mask is repaired segment by segment, last segment
859	    first.** Every row attends to a contiguous key prefix — its own index
860	    for a text token, its image block's last index for an image token — so
861	    the matrix-core pass still runs bidirectionally over the whole sequence
862	    (right for the target) and each prefix segment is then recomputed with
863	    its own key count. Backwards, because the WMMA kernel's query block
864	    starts at row 0 and an image segment's pass necessarily rewrites every
865	    row before it; running in reverse makes each row's last writer its own
866	    segment. It costs about a quarter again of the prefill's attention and
867	    needs no new matrix-core kernel.
868	  - **`dit_attn_causal.comp` became an online softmax** over chunks of keys,
869	    with a query-row offset and an optional fixed key count. That lifts the
870	    512-key cap it carried (a text run in the middle of an edit's prefix
871	    attends over the condition image before it) and costs nothing at t2i:
872	    for a prefix inside one chunk the arithmetic order is unchanged, and
873	    `TestGPUOracle256` comes back **bit-identical** (0.001503 / 0.00148
874	    before and after).
875	  - **The prefix KV cache moved into fp16 banks of its own**
876	    (`dit_kvcache.comp`). 32 blocks x 2 x 4136 rows x 4096 is **4.34 GB of
877	    fp32**, past this device's 4 GiB single-buffer cap; as halves it is
878	    **2.07 GB**, measured. The narrowing is *free*, not a trade: the pack
879	    narrows those rows to halves before attention reads them either way, so
880	    storing `fp32(fp16(x))` and packing it gives the same half.
881	
882	  **One real hazard came out of this, and it was worth the 4.9x**
883	  (`TAIL_MAX` in `dit_attention_wmma.comp`). The kernel masks keys past
884	  `pc.tokens` out of P but not out of the row *max*, which is sound in every
885	  existing caller because the packed plane is zeroed past the sequence — a
886	  key that does not exist scores 0 and can only set the scale on a row whose
887	  every real score is negative. The edit prefill's image-segment repair
888	  breaks that premise: it runs with the key count cut to a block's end, in
889	  the middle of a plane whose later rows are real and large. The softmax is
890	  shift-invariant so the answer stays right, but **P is stored in fp16**, and
891	  a max set by a key outside the mask shifts every real weight down before it
892	  is narrowed. A build with the mask reaching the max took the prefill step
893	  from **rel 0.0154 to 0.00314**. The mask has to reach the max to keep the
894	  precision, not to keep the answer.
895	  **Gate** (`TestGPUEditOracle`, against `out/qi21edit`, both regimes as the
896	  rule asks, the prompt embedding / condition latents / noise all the
897	  oracle's own so it is a gate on the transformer alone): teacher-forced
898	  **3.1e-3 at the prefill and 2.3e-4–1.4e-3 after it**, free-running
899	  **2.3e-3 over four steps**, against Q4's own bounds unchanged — an edit
900	  needed no bound of its own, because the arithmetic per row is identical and
901	  only the row count changed. Two runs identical. Three controls fire:
902	  condition latents zeroed **35x** the bound, the pad mask ignored so the
903	  condition never enters the sequence **54x**, and the block-causal repair
904	  switched off — the mask being wrong while every shape checks out —
905	  **29x**. And t2i is untouched, re-measured the same hour: 1024²/40 at
906	  **prefill 2.29 s, cached mean 2.27 s, 1m30.7s total**.
907	
908	  **Q8.6 — the edit pipeline and the endpoint. Done 2026-09-20**
909	  (`qimage/pipeline/edit.go`'s `Pipeline.Edit`, `backend.Image`, and
910	  `/v1/images/edits`). **A served edit at 1024² with one reference image is
911	  2m7.6s / 2m7.9s at 39.4 GB resident** — against a generation's 1m38s, which
912	  is the "slightly more expensive than a generation" this file predicted
913	  before any of it was built. By stage: the reference's own encoding 7.8 s
914	  (the vision tower 6.3, the VAE encoder 1.7), text encoding 0.73 s, prefill
915	  5.49 s, 40 cached steps at 2.70 s, decode 7.5 s.
916	  **The one thing that needed new infrastructure was the tower's sizing.**
917	  `vision.GPU` fixed its patch grid at construction, and a served edit hands
918	  it a different grid every request — `calculate_dimensions` fixes a
919	  reference's *area* and lets its sides follow its aspect ratio. It is now
920	  staged for a **patch budget** and takes the grid at `Forward`, which is the
921	  same split the VAE's graphs already made; `TestGPUTower` runs two
922	  differently-shaped cards through one staging and re-runs the first at
923	  **rel 0** to catch state left behind. Everything else composed: the VAE's
924	  GPU encoder already re-planned per image, and `Pipeline.Edit` is the eight
925	  stages the CPU gate composes with the device's versions substituted.
926	  **A second bound came out of the tower's sizing, and it is a finding.**
927	  `fp16Tol` was 0.25, measured by `TestFP16Ladder` on the square card. Run on
928	  the **wide** card the same ladder gives **0.297 / 0.438** — three times as
929	  much from the same weights and the same code — and the device lands at
930	  0.562 against that 0.438 prediction, the same agreement the square card
931	  shows (0.127 against 0.14). That is the fp16 face of what Q8.2 measured in
932	  fp32 (the dumped reference is itself 8.9e-4 from float64 on this card
933	  against 1.0e-4 on the square one): **some pictures amplify rounding an
934	  order of magnitude harder than others**, and a tower gated on one of them
935	  would be wrong about the other. Each card is now gated at its own
936	  measurement.
937	  **Gate** (`TestServedEditOracle256`, the edit twin of Q6's
938	  `TestServedOracle256`, both regimes): the whole request — the reference
939	  resized by our Lanczos port, composited over white on the 8-bit levels,
940	  through the GPU tower and the GPU VAE encoder, positioned by our mrope,
941	  injected into the GPU text encoder, laid out from the pad mask, denoised
942	  over a real prefix and decoded, only the noise the oracle's — reproduces
943	  the reference edit at **max abs 0.0014, mean 1.7e-4**. That is **24x
944	  tighter than the served t2i path's 0.0333**, for the reason Q8.3 found on
945	  the CPU: an edit's trajectory is pinned by its prefix where a generation's
946	  is free. Teacher-forced, the oracle's own latents decode at max abs
947	  0.00000. Controls: a blank white reference lands **366x** further out
948	  (measured against the run, not the bound), and two references on a
949	  one-reference server and an edit with no reference are both refusals.
950	  **The geometry needed one deviation from the reference, and it is named**
951	  (`targetFor`, `TestTargetFor`): `calculate_dimensions` fixes the *area* and
952	  lets the sides run, so at the shipped defaults — condition area and ceiling
953	  both 1024² — a 4:3 reference asks for 1184x896, whose long side is outside
954	  a 1024x1024 ceiling even though its area is not. Refusing would make every
955	  non-square edit a 400 out of the box; enlarging the ceiling would be
956	  residency nobody asked for. So the aspect ratio is kept and the area shrunk
957	  until both sides fit, and a ceiling above the condition area leaves
958	  diffusers' own answer untouched.
959	  **The endpoint's shape changed with the mechanism**, which is what Q6 said
960	  it would: `-edits` is now `-edits N` (residency — the tower and the VAE
961	  encoder are 1.4 GB, and each reference is ~2.1 GB of prefix KV cache at
962	  1024²), `image[]` is a real list, `strength` is a **400 that explains what
963	  changed** rather than a silently ignored field, `max_reference_images`
964	  joins the geometry in `GET /v1/models`, and an edit with no `size` follows
965	  the last reference's aspect ratio at the condition area instead of the
966	  server's default. Streaming needed no code: `partialSteps(0, …)` was
967	  already parameterised for an edit that starts at 0, which under 2.1 every
968	  edit does. Driven over HTTP end to end: a red mug becomes a blue mug on the
969	  same table with the same grain and the same light, and the streamed form
970	  sends two 32x32 partials and the finished 512².
971	- **Q9 — percents. First pass done 2026-09-20: the served image is 6% faster
972	  and the served edit 7%, bit for bit the same picture.** 1024²/40 goes
973	  **1m38.2s/1m41.3s → 1m32.3s/1m33.5s**, an edit **2m7.6s/2m7.9s →
974	  1m58.6s/1m59.2s**, and the DiT's cached step **2.27 s → 2.12–2.14 s**.
975	  Nothing about the numerics moved: `TestGPUOracle256` and the two served
976	  oracles return the same digits they did before (0.001503, max abs 0.0333,
977	  mean 3.4e-4).
978	  **The attribution came first and is the permanent instrument**
979	  (`TestGPUStepProfile`, both regimes at the served shape, one dispatch at a
980	  time). A cached step, before: **GEMMs 69% at 35–40 TFLOP/s**, attention
981	  10.6% at 37, and 21% in elementwise passes — pack 6.6%, swiglu 3.8%,
982	  qkpack 3.1%, gate 3.0%, the rest 4.2%. Q4 had run this graph on z-image's
983	  measured winners *uncontested*, and that is what the profile was for.
984	  **Two screens, and they disagreed about where the percent was.**
985	  - *The GEMM swizzle arm re-screen* — IMAGE.md's own hypothesis, since
986	    z-image chose SWZ=8 at M=16384/K=12288 and this model runs M=4096 —
987	    **found nothing, and that is the result** (`TestGPUGEMMScreen`, four arms
988	    on one staging): SWZ=8 wins here too, by 1.4–1.9% over SWZ=4 and 3.9–6.9%
989	    over the others, twice over. The GEMMs are at this kernel's ceiling and
990	    the inheritance was right.
991	  - *The fragment pack* was not a hypothesis anyone had, and it was the
992	    percent. The profile caught it moving **102 MB in 2.3 ms — 44 GB/s —
993	    where the SwiGLU dispatch beside it in the same block reaches 194** on
994	    the same bus. The layout it writes is why the matrix-core attention is
995	    worth using and was never in question; the *shape of the launch* was.
996	    One token tile per workgroup is 2048 elements over 256 threads — eight
997	    each, with two barriers around them — which is a latency-bound shape and
998	    not a bandwidth-bound one. `TPW` tiles per workgroup took the pack to
999	    **131 GB/s (3.0x)** and the fused q pack from 69 ms to 20, and the step
1000	    fell **5.9%** (`TestGPUPackScreen`, 1/2/4/8 arms). The screen asserts the
1001	    four arms' outputs **bit-identical** rather than close, because a screen
1002	    that only timed them could pick one that packs wrongly.
1003	  **What is left is at the bus, which is the next finding.** Re-profiled
1004	  after the fix, every remaining elementwise pass measures 190–194 GB/s:
1005	  swiglu 4.0%, gate 3.2%, pack 2.4%, narrow/rope/rmsnorm/ffn/attn 5.5%. None
1006	  of them is slow; there are simply round trips. So the next percents in the
1007	  DiT are *fusions* and are priced from the traffic they remove: the
1008	  attention writing its context straight into the o-projection's A operand
1009	  (z-image's stage-10 `OUT_F16`, the build already exists) is ~1%, and a
1010	  gated-accumulate GEMM epilogue that absorbs both residual adds is ~2% and
1011	  a new kernel. The GEMMs are 73% of what remains and at their ceiling.
1012	  **The bigger fish is elsewhere**: the VAE decode is 7.5 s of a 92 s image
1013	  and 68.8% of it is conv3x3 at 3.2 TFLOP/s, against the 38.3 the
1014	  matrix-core implicit GEMM measured in z-image with kernels already in this
1015	  tree. That is ~6 s, larger than anything left in the transformer, and it
1016	  is priced below.
1017	- **Q9's remaining ledger.** The I3/I5/I8/I9 fusion lesson
1018	  (elementwise passes absorbed into consumers) transfers to a new but
1019	  same-shaped budget; attribute before optimising, same-hour controls, plans
1020	  measured never composed. Two of them are already attributed and priced, by
1021	  `TestGPUDecodeProfile` on a 1024² decode (7.46 s one dispatch at a time):
1022	  - **conv3x3 is 68.8% — 5.13 s at 3.2 TFLOP/s**, which is z-image's stage-8
1023	    starting point to three digits (3.18 s, 3.0–3.2 TFLOP/s). That stage's
1024	    matrix-core implicit GEMM took it to 258 ms and 38.3 TFLOP/s, its
1025	    kernels and packing pass are already in the tree, and the range
1026	    measurement above says **every conv3x3 in this graph can feed it** —
1027	    the one convolution that cannot is a 1x1 shortcut worth a fraction of
1028	    the 3.8% that all four 1x1s cost together, and it simply stays scalar.
1029	    Expected: ~7.4 s → ~2.8 s.
1030	  - **the mid block's four projections are 21.0% — 1.57 s at 35 GFLOP/s** on
1031	    `vae_linear`, the same naive kernel and nearly the same number (62
1032	    GFLOP/s) that z-image's stage 7 replaced with `dit_gemm` unmodified.
1033	    Expected: another ~1.5 s.
1034	  Everything else in the decode is under 4%: attention 250 ms (the latent is
1035	  4096 rows here, not z-image's 16384 — this is *not* the 26% it was there),
1036	  chnorm 1.7% with its SiLU already fused, add 1.0%, the two shuffles 0.4%.
1037	
1038	  **What that port has to price first, and it is not in z-image's notes.**
1039	  Every percent taken on 2026-09-20 was **bit-identical** — a launch shape
1040	  and a kernel choice, no arithmetic moved. The conv port is not: the
1041	  matrix-core convolution narrows its *operands* to fp16, and this decoder's
1042	  convolutions read activations at **absmax 1.1e4** where z-image's peaked
1043	  at **497**. Both are inside half's 65504, so neither overflows and the
1044	  measurement that matters is not range but precision: an fp16 operand
1045	  carries ~5e-4 of relative error, and `vae_test.go`'s conv stages are gated
1046	  at **2e-4** with the decoded image at max abs 7.3e-4 against the dump.
1047	  So the port moves the numbers this vertical's tightest gates are written
1048	  against, and the first thing it owes is the same instrument every other
1049	  bound here came from — run the CPU decoder with fp16 conv operands and
1050	  fp32 accumulators, measure what it costs stagewise and on the image, and
1051	  gate the device at *that* rather than at the fp32 bounds it will not hold.
1052	  z-image made the same trade and kept its gates, but 20x less input range
1053	  is 20x less headroom, and assuming it transfers is exactly the composition
1054	  this file's method refuses. The infrastructure is otherwise ready:
1055	  `zimage/vae`'s `hbuf`/`w16buf` engine split, `vae_pack_conv.comp`,
1056	  nine `vae_conv_wmma` builds and `TestGPUConvMatchesScalar` are all in the
1057	  tree and are why `zimage/vae` was kept past its replacement.
1058	
1059	## Decisions taken now (so future sessions don't relitigate)
1060	
1061	1. **New `qimage/` tree; `zimage/qwen` and `zimage/tokenizer` stay put** until
1062	   z-image is fully gone, then a mechanical rename can hoist them.
1063	2. **KV cache always on** — validate against diffusers `use_kv_cache=True`;
1064	   cache-off exists only as a debug path if Q4 needs it.
1065	3. **Posterior mode (argmax) for every VAE encode** — matches the reference
1066	   and our reproducibility rule.
1067	4. **1024² default, 2048² behind the ceiling flag**, pending Q6's numbers —
1068	   amended 2026-09-20: 2048² is not a flag away. The decoder's arena stops
1069	   at **1184²** on one storage buffer (Q5g), so serving above that needs
1070	   tiling or a multi-buffer arena first. 1024² is the shipped default and
1071	   `-image-size` refuses anything larger than 1184x1184 at startup.
1072	5. **No self-trained tiny decoder**; linear preview + watch taehv.
1073	6. **No CFG path in the Go port** (true_cfg_scale stays a refusal if asked
1074	   for over HTTP) until something demands it — it would double every step.
1075	
1076	## Open questions
1077	
1078	- ~~**Q-o1**: how far below 40 steps does quality hold?~~ **Settled
1079	  2026-09-20 (Q6 sweep)**: it depends on the prompt, which is why the
1080	  default stays 40. Photographic and painterly prompts hold to **12 steps**
1081	  (36 s); a structured technical drawing is fine at 24 and broken at 12. The
1082	  headline is therefore **~1m38s at the safe default**, with 24 steps at
1083	  1m4s available to any client that sends `steps`.
1084	- **Q-o2**: does a turbo/distilled 2.1 checkpoint or step-distillation LoRA
1085	  appear? (Watch the examples repo and lightx2v.)
1086	- **Q-o3**: how are separate masks / painted annotations fed for local edits?
1087	  (Examples repo, before `/v1/images/edits` promises masks.)
1088	- **Q-o4**: does taehv grow a 2.1 variant? (Q7 fallback becomes an upgrade.)
1089	- ~~**Q-o5**: text-only mrope — confirmed equivalent to plain RoPE by dump?~~
1090	  **Settled 2026-09-20 (Q0)**: gap 0.0 against a plain theta-5e6 NeoX table;
1091	  `zimage/qwen` needs nothing mrope-shaped before Q8.

divides by the full group; and a second build of the attention kernel,
  because the encoder's mid block is **768** wide against the decoder's 1152
  (base_dim 96 against decoder_base_dim 144) and DIM is a shared-array
  extent rather than a push constant.
  The decoder and encoder now share an `engine` — buffers, pipelines,
  weights, arena — the same split `zimage/vae` made between its own two
  directions, so the second graph added no Vulkan lifecycle at all.
  **Gates**, on `vae_test.go`'s own bounds unchanged: every stage of both
  dump cases (conv_in, all five down blocks, the mid block, the fused tail
  norm, conv_out) and the posterior mode raw and normalised — **conv_in at
  1.1e-6 through to the mode at 2.6e-5** — plus a direct GPU-vs-CPU encode
  at **4.6e-5**. Two controls fire: the AvgDown temporal factor at
  **12173x** the bound (measured on the first block that *has* one — the
  checkpoint's `temperal_downsample` is [false, true, true, true], so
  breaking it and looking at block 0 shows nothing, which is how the control
  first passed for the wrong reason), and a symmetric-pad stride-2
  downsampler refused at construction rather than answered wrongly.

  **Q8.3d — the vision tower on the GPU. Done 2026-09-20**
  (`qimage/vision/gpu.go`, ~600 lines; `qvit_bias_act.comp` and
  `qvit_rope.comp` are the only new shaders). **A 1024² condition image runs
  the 27 blocks in 6.27 s** — two runs 6.283/6.265 — against roughly twenty
  minutes on the CPU port, and about 6% of an edit's total.
  **The precision was measured before it was chosen**, which is the part
  worth keeping. This tower sits between the tree's two conventions: the VAE
  is fp32 because its activations reach 1e5 against half's 65504, the DiT
  and text encoder are fp16 on the matrix cores because that is where their
  speed is, and this one's residual stream reaches absmax 1.3e4 — inside
  half's range but with three digits left — while Q8.2 measured the tower
  amplifying perturbations by ~1600x. So `TestFP16Ladder` runs the *CPU
  oracle* with every linear taking fp16 operands and accumulating in fp32,
  which is what a matrix core does, and reports **rel 0.135 at the last
  hidden state, 0.14 on the merged rows, no overflow** — sub-linear growth
  from 3.6e-3 at block 0. That is what said the matrix cores are usable, and
  it is the bound the port is gated at. The device then landed **within a
  few percent of the prediction at every stage** (merged 0.127 against 0.14,
  deepstack 0.016/0.031/0.050 against 0.015/0.035/0.053), which is better
  evidence of a correct port than the bound itself: a structural mistake in
  this tower moves these tensors by rel 0.76 to 8.1, per the four controls
  `qimage/vision` already carries.
  Almost every kernel is the DiT's, and three of the reuses are the reason
  the file is small. **The affine LayerNorm is `dit_final_norm` plus
  algebra**: that kernel computes LN(x)·scale, the ViT wants LN(x)·γ + β
  feeding W(·) + b, and W(LN(x)·γ + β) + b = W(LN(x)·γ) + (W·β + b) — so β
  is folded into the next projection's bias at load and the kernel is used
  verbatim. **The residual add is `dit_gate_add` with its gate dropped**,
  the path the DiT's two unmodulated blocks already take. **The patch
  merger's concatenation is free**: four consecutive rows of 1152 in a
  row-major buffer *are* one row of 4608, so the output merger normalises
  with a tight row stride and the GEMM reads the same bytes four rows at a
  time, while the three deepstack mergers normalise the 4608 directly.
  Attention is the **scalar** kernel, which takes its head width from a push
  constant and runs this tower's 72 unchanged; the matrix-core one is built
  per head dim and 72 does not divide its 16-wide tile. Padding to 80 would
  work and is a **percent, not a capability** — the 6.27 s says whether it is
  worth it, and at 6% of an edit it is not yet. The MLP's 4304 is padded to
  4352 for the same tile reason, with zeros that GELU fixes at zero and the
  second layer multiplies by zero rows.

  **Q8.4 — the edit text encoding on the GPU. Done 2026-09-20**
  (`qimage/textenc/edit.go`'s `EncodeGPU`, ~110 lines, plus four seams in
  `zimage/qwen`'s `GPUEncoder`). Q8.2's CPU path is minutes at a condition
  image's token count; this is **~0.12 s** at the dump's 99 and 177 rows, and
  it is what makes a served edit possible at all.
  **The transformer did not change.** The three mechanisms each landed on one
  seam, and the seams are the device counterparts of the three `ForwardEmbeds`
  grew in Q8.2: `Embeddings`+`UploadEmbeds` (the scatter is a host edit of
  the lookup, because the ids do not determine the rows), `SetRoPE` (the
  mrope table is uploaded rather than built as 0..T-1), and
  `RunHooked`+`AddRows` (the deepstack features are added at the pad slots
  between layers — one dispatch per image per layer, on `dit_gate_add` with
  its gate switched off, staged through the attention branch's own dead
  output tensor). `upload` is now `Embeddings` followed by `UploadEmbeds` and
  the plain table, so the t2i path runs the same code: `TestGPUEncoder`
  re-measures Q1's en/cjk/empty at **0.024 / 0.027 / 0.21, unchanged**.
  **Gates**, against `out/qi21vision` with the dump's *own* tower rows as the
  conditions (which makes it a gate on the text encoding rather than on the
  pair, exactly as Q8.2's two-image case argued): **one image 0.059, two
  images 0.064**, the pad mask exact, and layer 0 at **1.1e-3** against a
  4x bound — the shallow reading is what keeps a mistake in the three new
  mechanisms from hiding under the fp16 one. Controls: plain RoPE instead of
  mrope **133x** the bound, no deepstack injection **61x**, the conditions
  swapped refused at the row count. Two runs identical.
  **The bound is measured and it is 2.4x the t2i path's, and that is not a
  bug**: `TestGPUEditLadder` (the permanent instrument, `QI21_LADDER=1`,
  ~50 GB) walks the same run against the CPU port layer by layer and finds
  **Q1's mechanism unchanged and in the same place** — flat at ~1.1e-3 through
  layers 0-5, the massive-activation channel appearing at layer 6 (rms
  0.98 → 21.1) carrying an absolute error of 4.46 *flat*, a second jump at
  layer 16 whose 8.83 stays 8.83 **in the same column for 18 layers**, and
  then the cancellation in layers 34-35 surfacing it: 0.0049 → 0.0146 →
  0.0532. The last two layers are the whole of the deviation. And the
  *absolute* error does not move between the two paths at all — the worst
  element is **2.38 for the t2i prompt and for both edit prompts**, measured
  in the same hour; what the 2.4x buys is a different worst relative element
  under a lower rms floor. The official bf16 pipeline is rel 2.0 on this
  checkpoint, 30x further out.

  **Q8.5 — the DiT's edit path on the GPU. Done 2026-09-20**
  (`qimage/dit/gpu.go`, ~120 lines changed; `dit_kvcache.comp` and a rewrite
  of `dit_attn_causal.comp` are the shader work). **An edit's transformer at
  the served shape — a 1024² target on one 1024² reference — is prefill
  5.47/5.52 s and cached steps 2.70/2.71 s, so 40 steps is 110.7/111.3 s**
  against a generation's 90.7. That is the "slightly more expensive than a
  generation" this file predicted, now measured: +22%, all of it the prefix
  in every step's attention.
  Four things had to change, and three of them are about the prefix being
  thousands of rows instead of forty:
  - **The condition latents go through `img_in`.** They are latents in the
    same sequence, so they take the target's own projection — one GEMM per
    condition block off the same narrowed `aLat`, issued in ascending row
    order because a GEMM writes whole 128-row tiles and overruns a short
    block. The projected *text* rows then land by copy dispatch rather than
    by host write, since a host write cannot be ordered after a dispatch
    that has not been submitted.
  - **The block-causal mask is repaired segment by segment, last segment
    first.** Every row attends to a contiguous key prefix — its own index
    for a text token, its image block's last index for an image token — so
    the matrix-core pass still runs bidirectionally over the whole sequence
    (right for the target) and each prefix segment is then recomputed with
    its own key count. Backwards, because the WMMA kernel's query block
    starts at row 0 and an image segment's pass necessarily rewrites every
    row before it; running in reverse makes each row's last writer its own
    segment. It costs about a quarter again of the prefill's attention and
    needs no new matrix-core kernel.
  - **`dit_attn_causal.comp` became an online softmax** over chunks of keys,
    with a query-row offset and an optional fixed key count. That lifts the
    512-key cap it carried (a text run in the middle of an edit's prefix
    attends over the condition image before it) and costs nothing at t2i:
    for a prefix inside one chunk the arithmetic order is unchanged, and
    `TestGPUOracle256` comes back **bit-identical** (0.001503 / 0.00148
    before and after).
  - **The prefix KV cache moved into fp16 banks of its own**
    (`dit_kvcache.comp`). 32 blocks x 2 x 4136 rows x 4096 is **4.34 GB of
    fp32**, past this device's 4 GiB single-buffer cap; as halves it is
    **2.07 GB**, measured. The narrowing is *free*, not a trade: the pack
    narrows those rows to halves before attention reads them either way, so
    storing `fp32(fp16(x))` and packing it gives the same half.

  **One real hazard came out of this, and it was worth the 4.9x**
  (`TAIL_MAX` in `dit_attention_wmma.comp`). The kernel masks keys past
  `pc.tokens` out of P but not out of the row *max*, which is sound in every
  existing caller because the packed plane is zeroed past the sequence — a
  key that does not exist scores 0 and can only set the scale on a row whose
  every real score is negative. The edit prefill's image-segment repair
  breaks that premise: it runs with the key count cut to a block's end, in
  the middle of a plane whose later rows are real and large. The softmax is
  shift-invariant so the answer stays right, but **P is stored in fp16**, and
  a max set by a key outside the mask shifts every real weight down before it
  is narrowed. A build with the mask reaching the max took the prefill step
  from **rel 0.0154 to 0.00314**. The mask has to reach the max to keep the
  precision, not to keep the answer.
  **Gate** (`TestGPUEditOracle`, against `out/qi21edit`, both regimes as the
  rule asks, the prompt embedding / condition latents / noise all the
  oracle's own so it is a gate on the transformer alone): teacher-forced
  **3.1e-3 at the prefill and 2.3e-4–1.4e-3 after it**, free-running
  **2.3e-3 over four steps**, against Q4's own bounds unchanged — an edit
  needed no bound of its own, because the arithmetic per row is identical and
  only the row count changed. Two runs identical. Three controls fire:
  condition latents zeroed **35x** the bound, the pad mask ignored so the
  condition never enters the sequence **54x**, and the block-causal repair
  switched off — the mask being wrong while every shape checks out —
  **29x**. And t2i is untouched, re-measured the same hour: 1024²/40 at
  **prefill 2.29 s, cached mean 2.27 s, 1m30.7s total**.

  **Q8.6 — the edit pipeline and the endpoint. Done 2026-09-20**
  (`qimage/pipeline/edit.go`'s `Pipeline.Edit`, `backend.Image`, and
  `/v1/images/edits`). **A served edit at 1024² with one reference image is
  2m7.6s / 2m7.9s at 39.4 GB resident** — against a generation's 1m38s, which
  is the "slightly more expensive than a generation" this file predicted
  before any of it was built. By stage: the reference's own encoding 7.8 s
  (the vision tower 6.3, the VAE encoder 1.7), text encoding 0.73 s, prefill
  5.49 s, 40 cached steps at 2.70 s, decode 7.5 s.
  **The one thing that needed new infrastructure was the tower's sizing.**
  `vision.GPU` fixed its patch grid at construction, and a served edit hands
  it a different grid every request — `calculate_dimensions` fixes a
  reference's *area* and lets its sides follow its aspect ratio. It is now
  staged for a **patch budget** and takes the grid at `Forward`, which is the
  same split the VAE's graphs already made; `TestGPUTower` runs two
  differently-shaped cards through one staging and re-runs the first at
  **rel 0** to catch state left behind. Everything else composed: the VAE's
  GPU encoder already re-planned per image, and `Pipeline.Edit` is the eight
  stages the CPU gate composes with the device's versions substituted.
  **A second bound came out of the tower's sizing, and it is a finding.**
  `fp16Tol` was 0.25, measured by `TestFP16Ladder` on the square card. Run on
  the **wide** card the same ladder gives **0.297 / 0.438** — three times as
  much from the same weights and the same code — and the device lands at
  0.562 against that 0.438 prediction, the same agreement the square card
  shows (0.127 against 0.14). That is the fp16 face of what Q8.2 measured in
  fp32 (the dumped reference is itself 8.9e-4 from float64 on this card
  against 1.0e-4 on the square one): **some pictures amplify rounding an
  order of magnitude harder than others**, and a tower gated on one of them
  would be wrong about the other. Each card is now gated at its own
  measurement.
  **Gate** (`TestServedEditOracle256`, the edit twin of Q6's
  `TestServedOracle256`, both regimes): the whole request — the reference
  resized by our Lanczos port, composited over white on the 8-bit levels,
  through the GPU tower and the GPU VAE encoder, positioned by our mrope,
  injected into the GPU text encoder, laid out from the pad mask, denoised
  over a real prefix and decoded, only the noise the oracle's — reproduces
  the reference edit at **max abs 0.0014, mean 1.7e-4**. That is **24x
  tighter than the served t2i path's 0.0333**, for the reason Q8.3 found on
  the CPU: an edit's trajectory is pinned by its prefix where a generation's
  is free. Teacher-forced, the oracle's own latents decode at max abs
  0.00000. Controls: a blank white reference lands **366x** further out
  (measured against the run, not the bound), and two references on a
  one-reference server and an edit with no reference are both refusals.
  **The geometry needed one deviation from the reference, and it is named**
  (`targetFor`, `TestTargetFor`): `calculate_dimensions` fixes the *area* and
  lets the sides run, so at the shipped defaults — condition area and ceiling
  both 1024² — a 4:3 reference asks for 1184x896, whose long side is outside
  a 1024x1024 ceiling even though its area is not. Refusing would make every
  non-square edit a 400 out of the box; enlarging the ceiling would be
  residency nobody asked for. So the aspect ratio is kept and the area shrunk
  until both sides fit, and a ceiling above the condition area leaves
  diffusers' own answer untouched.
  **The endpoint's shape changed with the mechanism**, which is what Q6 said
  it would: `-edits` is now `-edits N` (residency — the tower and the VAE
  encoder are 1.4 GB, and each reference is ~2.1 GB of prefix KV cache at
  1024²), `image[]` is a real list, `strength` is a **400 that explains what
  changed** rather than a silently ignored field, `max_reference_images`
  joins the geometry in `GET /v1/models`, and an edit with no `size` follows
  the last reference's aspect ratio at the condition area instead of the
  server's default. Streaming needed no code: `partialSteps(0, …)` was
  already parameterised for an edit that starts at 0, which under 2.1 every
  edit does. Driven over HTTP end to end: a red mug becomes a blue mug on the
  same table with the same grain and the same light, and the streamed form
  sends two 32x32 partials and the finished 512².
- **Q9 — percents. First pass done 2026-09-20: the served image is 6% faster
  and the served edit 7%, bit for bit the same picture.** 1024²/40 goes
  **1m38.2s/1m41.3s → 1m32.3s/1m33.5s**, an edit **2m7.6s/2m7.9s →
  1m58.6s/1m59.2s**, and the DiT's cached step **2.27 s → 2.12–2.14 s**.
  Nothing about the numerics moved: `TestGPUOracle256` and the two served
  oracles return the same digits they did before (0.001503, max abs 0.0333,
  mean 3.4e-4).
  **The attribution came first and is the permanent instrument**
  (`TestGPUStepProfile`, both regimes at the served shape, one dispatch at a
  time). A cached step, before: **GEMMs 69% at 35–40 TFLOP/s**, attention
  10.6% at 37, and 21% in elementwise passes — pack 6.6%, swiglu 3.8%,
  qkpack 3.1%, gate 3.0%, the rest 4.2%. Q4 had run this graph on z-image's
  measured winners *uncontested*, and that is what the profile was for.
  **Two screens, and they disagreed about where the percent was.**
  - *The GEMM swizzle arm re-screen* — IMAGE.md's own hypothesis, since
    z-image chose SWZ=8 at M=16384/K=12288 and this model runs M=4096 —
    **found nothing, and that is the result** (`TestGPUGEMMScreen`, four arms
    on one staging): SWZ=8 wins here too, by 1.4–1.9% over SWZ=4 and 3.9–6.9%
    over the others, twice over. The GEMMs are at this kernel's ceiling and
    the inheritance was right.
  - *The fragment pack* was not a hypothesis anyone had, and it was the
    percent. The profile caught it moving **102 MB in 2.3 ms — 44 GB/s —
    where the SwiGLU dispatch beside it in the same block reaches 194** on
    the same bus. The layout it writes is why the matrix-core attention is
    worth using and was never in question; the *shape of the launch* was.
    One token tile per workgroup is 2048 elements over 256 threads — eight
    each, with two barriers around them — which is a latency-bound shape and
    not a bandwidth-bound one. `TPW` tiles per workgroup took the pack to
    **131 GB/s (3.0x)** and the fused q pack from 69 ms to 20, and the step
    fell **5.9%** (`TestGPUPackScreen`, 1/2/4/8 arms). The screen asserts the
    four arms' outputs **bit-identical** rather than close, because a screen
    that only timed them could pick one that packs wrongly.
  **What is left is at the bus, which is the next finding.** Re-profiled
  after the fix, every remaining elementwise pass measures 190–194 GB/s:
  swiglu 4.0%, gate 3.2%, pack 2.4%, narrow/rope/rmsnorm/ffn/attn 5.5%. None
  of them is slow; there are simply round trips. So the next percents in the
  DiT are *fusions* and are priced from the traffic they remove: the
  attention writing its context straight into the o-projection's A operand
  (z-image's stage-10 `OUT_F16`, the build already exists) is ~1%, and a
  gated-accumulate GEMM epilogue that absorbs both residual adds is ~2% and
  a new kernel. The GEMMs are 73% of what remains and at their ceiling.
  **The bigger fish is elsewhere**: the VAE decode is 7.5 s of a 92 s image
  and 68.8% of it is conv3x3 at 3.2 TFLOP/s, against the 38.3 the
  matrix-core implicit GEMM measured in z-image with kernels already in this
  tree. That is ~6 s, larger than anything left in the transformer, and it
  is priced below.
- **Q9's remaining ledger.** The I3/I5/I8/I9 fusion lesson
  (elementwise passes absorbed into consumers) transfers to a new but
  same-shaped budget; attribute before optimising, same-hour controls, plans
  measured never composed. Two of them are already attributed and priced, by
  `TestGPUDecodeProfile` on a 1024² decode (7.46 s one dispatch at a time):
  - **conv3x3 is 68.8% — 5.13 s at 3.2 TFLOP/s**, which is z-image's stage-8
    starting point to three digits (3.18 s, 3.0–3.2 TFLOP/s). That stage's
    matrix-core implicit GEMM took it to 258 ms and 38.3 TFLOP/s, its
    kernels and packing pass are already in the tree, and the range
    measurement above says **every conv3x3 in this graph can feed it** —
    the one convolution that cannot is a 1x1 shortcut worth a fraction of
    the 3.8% that all four 1x1s cost together, and it simply stays scalar.
    Expected: ~7.4 s → ~2.8 s.
  - **the mid block's four projections are 21.0% — 1.57 s at 35 GFLOP/s** on
    `vae_linear`, the same naive kernel and nearly the same number (62
    GFLOP/s) that z-image's stage 7 replaced with `dit_gemm` unmodified.
    Expected: another ~1.5 s.
  Everything else in the decode is under 4%: attention 250 ms (the latent is
  4096 rows here, not z-image's 16384 — this is *not* the 26% it was there),
  chnorm 1.7% with its SiLU already fused, add 1.0%, the two shuffles 0.4%.

  **What that port has to price first, and it is not in z-image's notes.**
  Every percent taken on 2026-09-20 was **bit-identical** — a launch shape
  and a kernel choice, no arithmetic moved. The conv port is not: the
  matrix-core convolution narrows its *operands* to fp16, and this decoder's
  convolutions read activations at **absmax 1.1e4** where z-image's peaked
  at **497**. Both are inside half's 65504, so neither overflows and the
  measurement that matters is not range but precision: an fp16 operand
  carries ~5e-4 of relative error, and `vae_test.go`'s conv stages are gated
  at **2e-4** with the decoded image at max abs 7.3e-4 against the dump.
  So the port moves the numbers this vertical's tightest gates are written
  against, and the first thing it owes is the same instrument every other
  bound here came from — run the CPU decoder with fp16 conv operands and
  fp32 accumulators, measure what it costs stagewise and on the image, and
  gate the device at *that* rather than at the fp32 bounds it will not hold.
  z-image made the same trade and kept its gates, but 20x less input range
  is 20x less headroom, and assuming it transfers is exactly the composition
  this file's method refuses. The infrastructure is otherwise ready:
  `zimage/vae`'s `hbuf`/`w16buf` engine split, `vae_pack_conv.comp`,
  nine `vae_conv_wmma` builds and `TestGPUConvMatchesScalar` are all in the
  tree and are why `zimage/vae` was kept past its replacement.

## Decisions taken now (so future sessions don't relitigate)

1. **New `qimage/` tree; `zimage/qwen` and `zimage/tokenizer` stay put** until
   z-image is fully gone, then a mechanical rename can hoist them.
2. **KV cache always on** — validate against diffusers `use_kv_cache=True`;
   cache-off exists only as a debug path if Q4 needs it.
3. **Posterior mode (argmax) for every VAE encode** — matches the reference
   and our reproducibility rule.
4. **1024² default, 2048² behind the ceiling flag**, pending Q6's numbers —
   amended 2026-09-20: 2048² is not a flag away. The decoder's arena stops
   at **1184²** on one storage buffer (Q5g), so serving above that needs
   tiling or a multi-buffer arena first. 1024² is the shipped default and
   `-image-size` refuses anything larger than 1184x1184 at startup.
5. **No self-trained tiny decoder**; linear preview + watch taehv.
6. **No CFG path in the Go port** (true_cfg_scale stays a refusal if asked
   for over HTTP) until something demands it — it would double every step.

## Open questions

- ~~**Q-o1**: how far below 40 steps does quality hold?~~ **Settled
  2026-09-20 (Q6 sweep)**: it depends on the prompt, which is why the
  default stays 40. Photographic and painterly prompts hold to **12 steps**
  (36 s); a structured technical drawing is fine at 24 and broken at 12. The
  headline is therefore **~1m38s at the safe default**, with 24 steps at
  1m4s available to any client that sends `steps`.
- **Q-o2**: does a turbo/distilled 2.1 checkpoint or step-distillation LoRA
  appear? (Watch the examples repo and lightx2v.)
- **Q-o3**: how are separate masks / painted annotations fed for local edits?
  (Examples repo, before `/v1/images/edits` promises masks.)
- **Q-o4**: does taehv grow a 2.1 variant? (Q7 fallback becomes an upgrade.)
- ~~**Q-o5**: text-only mrope — confirmed equivalent to plain RoPE by dump?~~
  **Settled 2026-09-20 (Q0)**: gap 0.0 against a plain theta-5e6 NeoX table;
  `zimage/qwen` needs nothing mrope-shaped before Q8.

**What that port has to price first, and it is not in z-image's notes.**
  Every percent taken on 2026-09-20 was **bit-identical** — a launch shape
  and a kernel choice, no arithmetic moved. The conv port is not: the
  matrix-core convolution narrows its *operands* to fp16, and this decoder's
  convolutions read activations at **absmax 1.1e4** where z-image's peaked
  at **497**. Both are inside half's 65504, so neither overflows and the
  measurement that matters is not range but precision: an fp16 operand
  carries ~5e-4 of relative error, and `vae_test.go`'s conv stages are gated
  at **2e-4** with the decoded image at max abs 7.3e-4 against the dump.
  So the port moves the numbers this vertical's tightest gates are written
  against, and the first thing it owes is the same instrument every other
  bound here came from — run the CPU decoder with fp16 conv operands and
  fp32 accumulators, measure what it costs stagewise and on the image, and
  gate the device at *that* rather than at the fp32 bounds it will not hold.
  z-image made the same trade and kept its gates, but 20x less input range
  is 20x less headroom, and assuming it transfers is exactly the composition
  this file's method refuses. The infrastructure is otherwise ready:
  `zimage/vae`'s `hbuf`/`w16buf` engine split, `vae_pack_conv.comp`,
  nine `vae_conv_wmma` builds and `TestGPUConvMatchesScalar` are all in the
  tree and are why `zimage/vae` was kept past its replacement.

input.new_string:
nine `vae_conv_wmma` builds and `TestGPUConvMatchesScalar` are all in the
  tree and are why `zimage/vae` was kept past its replacement.
- **Q10 — the ceiling is an area, not a box. Done 2026-09-21**, and it came
  out of a served complaint rather than a plan: a 16:9 request against the
  shipped server was answering **1024x576**, 0.59 Mpx, where the same arenas
  hold 1.05. Nothing was broken — `fitRatio` was fitting the ratio inside
  `MaxWidth`/`MaxHeight` exactly as written — the *rule* was wrong, and it
  was wrong because it was inherited.
  **The measurement first** (`qimage/vae`'s `TestArenaShape`, the permanent
  instrument): plan the decode for a dozen shapes and the activation arena is
  **exactly 3060 bytes a pixel for every one of them** — 1024x1024, 1344x768,
  2048x512, 256x4096, 4096x256, to the byte, with no per-axis term at all.
  The DiT's rows are the pixel count over 256 by construction and the text
  encoder does not see the geometry, so **residency in this pipeline is a
  function of area alone**. The side box came from `api.ImageGeometry`'s
  z-image-era doc, which argued the opposite and was *right about z-image*:
  that VAE holds blocked fp16 copies of each convolution's input, padded per
  axis, so 128x512 genuinely cost it more than 256x256. Q5g's decoder keeps
  its activations flat. The constraint was carried across with the comment
  that justified it and never re-measured — the same composition-without-
  measurement this file's method refuses everywhere else.
  **What it cost, and it is the largest single number this vertical has
  moved**: at the shipped 1024² ceiling, `aspect_ratio: "16:9"` goes
  **1024x576 → 1344x768 (1.75x the pixels)**, 3:2 → 1248x832 (1.51x), 21:9 →
  1536x672 (2.42x), and an edit that names no size goes 1024x768 → 1152x896
  on a 4:3 reference. At the hardware's own ceiling (`-image-size 1184x1184`,
  1,403,584 px) 16:9 is **1536x864**, which is 2.25x what the box gave.
  **And it is free**, which is the point: a 1344x768 image is 4032 latent
  tokens against a square's 4096, so it costs *less* than the picture it
  replaces. Measured on the device at 8 steps, one square staging serving all
  four shapes: 1024x1024 27.0 s, **1344x768 26.5 s**, 768x1344 26.4 s,
  2048x512 27.0 s, steps flat at 2.36 s (`TestGeometryShapes`, the graph gate
  the new regime needed — arithmetic could not have settled whether a
  re-planned decode and a non-square RoPE grid actually run, and a transposed
  grid would produce a plausible tensor, so the PNGs are written and looked
  at).
  **The fit had to grow a rule**, because the grid is coarse: both sides are
  multiples of 32 px, so an exact 16:9 exists only at 512m x 288m and there is
  nothing between 1024x576 and 1536x864. `fitAspect` now maximises the area
  **of the shape that was asked for** — a candidate's area discounted by what
  survives a centre-crop back to the requested ratio — with near-ties (within
  0.5%) broken toward the closer ratio. That is what picks 1344x768 at 1.05
  Mpx and the *exact* 1536x864 at 1.40, where a plain "largest that fits"
  would have taken 1568x864 and been 2% wider than asked.
  Two things deliberately did not change: the hard limit is still the VAE's
  single storage buffer (now stated as **1,403,584 pixels** rather than
  1184x1184, which is the same number said correctly), and `-image-size` is
  still one flag naming both the default size and the ceiling — its *area* is
  now what the ceiling means.

`KPipeline.load_voice` gives that spelling exactly that meaning, so the same
request is the same voice here as anywhere else kokoro runs (research/speech-vertical.md T8).
`"af_bella:3,af_sky:1"` weights the mix, which is ours, and the weights are
normalised by their sum so they need not add up. Either every component
carries a weight or none does: `"af_bella:0.7,af_sky"` is a 400, because it
reads as either 0.3 for the rest or one share before normalising and a mix
that guessed would still sound like a voice. An unknown name is a 400 naming
*which component* was unknown, since that is the one thing a three-part string
does not tell you. The `voices` array stays the list of single names: a blend
is every comma-joined subset of them and not a list anything could enumerate.

`POST /v1/images/generations` takes three fields that are not OpenAI's, and
each of them exists because the parameter is real here and there is nowhere
else to put it. **`"seed"`** names the initial latent's seed, and a response
reports the seed whether or not the request named one — a drawn seed that the
client is not told is an image that cannot be asked for twice. **`"steps"`**
is the denoising schedule's length, which is a host-side array and therefore
genuinely per request. And **`"aspect_ratio"`** — `"16:9"` and the like — is
fitted to the largest image *this* server holds, so a client wanting a
landscape picture does not have to know the ceiling to ask for one; `size`
wins when both are set, because that is the field every other server reads.
`GET /v1/models` carries an **`image`** object on the image model, alongside
the speech model's voices and for the same reason: `default_size`, `max_size`,
`size_multiple`, `default_steps`, `previews`, `max_partial_images`, `edits` and
`max_reference_images`, which are decided by what this process staged. The
last four are how a client finds out that `stream: true` and an edit will be
answered, and with how many pictures, rather than discovering it from a 501.

**`background: "transparent"` is OpenAI's field and it is answerable here**,
because Qwen-Image-2.1's VAE is natively RGBA — four channels out of the
decoder on every image. It is not a mode, though, and that is the part worth
knowing: what actually makes a background transparent is *asking for it in
the prompt*, so the server prepends and appends the checkpoint's own
recommended phrasing ("This is an RGBA image with transparency. … The image
has alpha channel and the background is transparent.") and keeps the alpha
plane. `"opaque"` and `"auto"` leave the prompt alone and composite the
result over white, which is what an ordinary picture wants — the alpha plane
exists either way and on an ordinary prompt it is whatever the model painted
there. `background: "transparent"` with `output_format: "jpeg"` is a 400
naming both fields rather than a silently flattened image.

Done. Here's what was wrong and what changed.

## The diagnosis

Your logic was self-consistent but built on an inherited constraint that isn't true of this model. `api.ImageGeometry` capped **each side** (`MaxWidth`/`MaxHeight`), so `aspect_ratio: "16:9"` against a `-image-size 1024x1024` server fit 16:9 inside a 1024×1024 *box* → 1024x576. Your live service confirms it — `journalctl` shows `out 1024x576` on tonight's edits.

The side limit came from the Z-Image era, where it was correct: that VAE held blocked fp16 conv copies padded per axis, so 128x512 really did cost more arena than 256x256. The Qwen-Image-2.1 decoder keeps its activations flat. I measured rather than argued — planning the decode graph for a dozen shapes:

```
1024x1024  3060 MB   1344x768  3012 MB   2048x512  3060 MB
 256x4096  3060 MB   4096x256  3060 MB   1184x1184 4090 MB
```

**Exactly 3060 bytes per pixel, every aspect ratio, to the byte.** The DiT's rows are pixels/256 by construction. So residency is area, full stop — the side cap was taxing every landscape request for nothing.

## The change

The ceiling is now a pixel budget; the shape is free. At the shipped `1024x1024`:

| request | was | now | pixels |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16:9 | 1024x576 | **1344x768** | 1.75x |
| 3:2 | 1024x672 | 1248x832 | 1.51x |
| 21:9 | 1024x416 | 1536x672 | 2.42x |
| 4:3 edit, no size | 1024x768 | 1152x896 | 1.27x |

`fitAspect` maximises the area *of the shape asked for* (area discounted by what survives a crop back to the ratio), because the 32-px grid is coarse — that's what picks 1344x768 at 1.05 Mpx and the exact 1536x864 at 1.40 rather than something 2% too wide.

**And it's free**: 1344x768 is 4032 latent tokens against the square's 4096, so it costs *less* than the picture it replaces. Device gate (`TestGeometryShapes`, one square staging serving all four shapes, 8 steps): 1024² 27.0 s, 1344x768 26.5 s, 768x1344 26.4 s, 2048x512 27.0 s, step flat at 2.36 s. A full 40-step 16:9 is in `out/qi21served/served1344x768_40steps.png` at 1m44 — the 14% over Q9's 1m32 is contention, your `ai` service was resident and serving while it ran.

## On >2K

Not reachable today, and it's not the geometry — it's the VAE. Its activation arena is one storage buffer and this device caps one at 4 GiB−4, i.e. **1,403,584 pixels**. 2048x1152 wants 6885 MB. So the real ceilings are `-image-size 1184x1184` → 1184² square or **1536x864** at 16:9 (2.25x what you're getting now). Past that needs tiled decode or a descriptor-array arena — a capability, already written up as such in IMAGE.md.

Gates added: `TestArenaShape` (the measurement the policy rests on), `TestGeometryShapes` (the graph gate for the new regime), plus rewritten `TestAspectRatioFitsTheCeiling`/`TestTargetFor`. `IMAGE.md` has it as Q10, `API.md` documents `max_pixels` beside `max_size`.

Two things for you to decide: the running service still has the old binary, so want me to rebuild and restart it? And `-image-size` still sets default *and* ceiling from one flag — if you want the 1.40 Mpx ceiling without making 1184² the default for requests that name no size, that needs a second flag, which I didn't add unasked.

content.text:
Checked each path rather than trusting the comments. **Short answer: no for the image run — it goes to completion. The LLM does cancel properly.**

## Images

`backend.Image.Generate` checks `ctx.Err()` once on entry (`backend/image.go:211`) and never again. Below that there's no context at all: `pipeline.Run`, `Edit` and `denoise` don't take one — the step loop at `qimage/pipeline/gpu.go:544` has no cancellation point in it. So a client that hangs up mid-run still costs the full ~92 s of DiT plus the 7.5 s decode, and for an edit the vision tower and VAE encode on top.

Three things *are* respected, none of which stops the run in progress:

- **The entry check** — a request queued behind another one is dropped the moment it reaches the head of the backend lock, without touching the device.
- **`n > 1`** — each image is a separate `Generate` call, so a cancelled 4-image request stops after the current picture rather than after the fourth.
- **Streaming partials** — `sendPartial` checks `r.Context()` (`api/images.go:463`), so frames stop going out and `perr` becomes what `Generate` returns. That's reporting, not stopping; it saves 159 µs a frame.

The reasoning in the code is sound as far as it goes: a denoising step is a submit-and-fence, and returning early from inside `Device.Do` would leave the device mid-graph. But that argument only justifies not aborting *within* a step.

## The others

| backend | granularity |
|---|---|
| LLM | **real** — `ctx.Err()` between decode tokens (`llm.go:320`) and between prefill chunks (`llm.go:479`) |
| Embed | between inputs (`embed.go:139`), so a batch stops early |
| TTS, STT | entry only, same bargain as images |

## What it costs beyond wasted GPU

`backend.Device.mu` is a single global lock across *all* verticals — the image run holds it end to end. So an abandoned 1024²/40 doesn't just waste 100 s of its own, it blocks every queued TTS, STT and embedding request behind it for the full duration.

The fix is small and the boundary already exists: 40 discrete submit+fence steps at ~2.2 s each. Threading a context through `Request`/`EditRequest` into `denoise` and checking between steps bounds the waste at one step instead of a whole image, and releases the device lock. The VAE decode would stay uninterruptible unless I also add a check between its dispatch batches — worth doing at the same time, it's another 7.5 s.

Want me to implement that? It's contained: the two pipeline entry points, the denoise loop, and one line in `backend/image.go` to pass `r.Context()` through.

135	// 3x3 stride-2 convolution over a (0, 1, 0, 1)-padded input computes exactly

42	// from zero — math.RoundToEven and not math.Round. It only bites on exact
43	// halves, which at this granularity means a source whose scaled side lands
44	// on a multiple of 16 that is not one of 32; rare, and free to get right.
45	func CalcDimensions(targetArea int, ratio float64) (int, int) {
46		w := math.Sqrt(float64(targetArea) * ratio)

56		out := qwen.NewMat(z.H*z.W, z.C)
57		for c := 0; c < z.C; c++ {

1	// Command qimage generates an image with Qwen-Image-2.1 on the device, which
2	// is what cmd/zimage was for Z-Image-Turbo (IMAGE.md Q6).
3	//
4	//	go run ./cmd/qimage -prompt "a red fox in fresh snow" -out fox.png
5	//	go run ./cmd/qimage -steps 16 -reps 2            # the step/wall-clock trade
6	//	go run ./cmd/qimage -width 512 -height 768       # a portrait, inside the ceiling
7	//	go run ./cmd/qimage -transparent -out sticker.png
8	//
9	// It is the tool the step-count sweep and the eyeball are done with, so it
10	// reports the wall clock by stage rather than only the total: the text
11	// encoder, the DiT's prefill, the mean cached step, and the VAE. Those four
12	// are what IMAGE.md's per-stage numbers are made of.
13	//
14	// **The size is a request parameter, the ceiling is residency.** -width and
15	// -height set both here, because a one-shot command has no reason to build
16	// arenas larger than the image it was asked for. The ceiling is an *area*
17	// rather than a rectangle -- every arena is sized by the pixel count alone,
18	// measured -- and it stops at 1,403,584 pixels (1184x1184 square, 1536x864 at
19	// 16:9): the VAE decoder's activation arena is one storage buffer and this
20	// device caps one at 4 GiB - 4.
21	package main
22	
23	import (
24		"flag"
25		"fmt"
26		"image/png"
27		"log"
28		"os"
29		"time"
30	
31		"strix-halo-vulkan/qimage/pipeline"
32		"strix-halo-vulkan/vk"
33		zvae "strix-halo-vulkan/zimage/vae"
34	)
35	
36	const strixHaloDeviceID = 0x1586
37	
38	func main() {
39		log.SetFlags(0)
40		model := flag.String("model", "models/Qwen-Image-2.1", "checkpoint root")
41		prompt := flag.String("prompt", "a red fox sitting in fresh snow at dawn, photograph, shallow depth of field", "the prompt")
42		out := flag.String("out", "qimage.png", "PNG to write; with -reps > 1 the repetition index is appended")
43		width := flag.Int("width", 1024, "image width in pixels, a multiple of 32")
44		height := flag.Int("height", 0, "image height; 0 is square")
45		steps := flag.Int("steps", pipeline.DefaultSteps, "denoising steps; the checkpoint's default is 40")
46		seed := flag.Int64("seed", 1, "seed for the initial latent")
47		maxPrompt := flag.Int("maxprompt", 512, "longest prompt the text encoder is built for")
48		reps := flag.Int("reps", 1, "generate this many times, reporting each; the first also pays the arenas' first touch")
49		transparent := flag.Bool("transparent", false,
50			"ask for an RGBA image with a transparent background, using the model card's recommended prompt phrasing")
51		progress := flag.Bool("progress", false, "log every denoising step as it lands")
52		flag.Parse()
53	
54		if *height == 0 {
55			*height = *width
56		}
57		text := *prompt
58		if *transparent {
59			text = "This is an RGBA image with transparency. " + text +
60				" The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent."
61		}
62	
63		inst, err := vk.NewInstance("qimage")
64		must(err)
65		defer inst.Destroy()
66		devs, err := inst.PhysicalDevices()
67		must(err)
68		phys := &devs[0]
69		for i := range devs {
70			if devs[i].DeviceID == strixHaloDeviceID {
71				phys = &devs[i]
72			}
73		}
74		qf, err := phys.ComputeQueueFamily()
75		must(err)
76		sgs, err := phys.SubgroupSizeControl()
77		must(err)
78		dev, err := vk.NewDevice(phys, qf, vk.DeviceFeatures{
79			Float16: true, CoopMatrix: true, SubgroupSizeControl: sgs.Supported,
80		})
81		must(err)
82		defer dev.Destroy()
83	
84		fmt.Printf("device: %s\n", phys.Name)
85		fmt.Printf("%dx%d, %d steps, seed %d\n", *width, *height, *steps, *seed)
86	
87		t0 := time.Now()
88		p, err := pipeline.New(dev, pipeline.Options{
89			Model: *model, Width: *width, Height: *height, Steps: *steps, MaxPrompt: *maxPrompt,
90		})
91		must(err)
92		defer p.Destroy()
93		enc, dt, vaeW, act := p.Residency()
94		fmt.Printf("staged in %v: %.1f GB (%.1f encoder + %.1f transformer + %.1f vae + %.1f activations)\n",
95			time.Since(t0).Round(time.Millisecond), float64(enc+dt+vaeW+act)/1e9,
96			float64(enc)/1e9, float64(dt)/1e9, float64(vaeW)/1e9, float64(act)/1e9)
97	
98		for rep := 0; rep < *reps; rep++ {
99			var onStep func(pipeline.Step)
100			if *progress {
101				onStep = func(st pipeline.Step) {
102					fmt.Printf("  step %2d/%d  %7.1f ms  sigma %.4f -> %.4f\n",
103						st.Index, st.Steps, float64(st.Wall.Microseconds())/1000, st.Sigma, st.NextSigma)
104				}
105			}
106			img, tm, err := p.Run(ctx, pipeline.Request{
107				Prompt: text, Width: *width, Height: *height, Steps: *steps,
108				Seed: *seed + int64(rep), Progress: onStep,
109			})
110			must(err)
111			report(tm)
112			path := *out
113			if *reps > 1 {
114				path = fmt.Sprintf("%s.%d.png", *out, rep)
115			}
116			must(writePNG(path, img, !*transparent))
117			fmt.Printf("wrote %s\n", path)
118		}
119	}
120	
121	// report is the per-stage wall clock, which is the point of this command.
122	// The prefill is separated from the cached steps because they are different
123	// work: step 0 runs the whole joint sequence block-causally and stores every
124	// block's prefix K/V, and the rest recompute only the target's rows.
125	func report(tm *pipeline.Timings) {
126		var cached time.Duration
127		for _, d := range tm.Steps[1:] {
128			cached += d
129		}
130		mean := time.Duration(0)
131		if len(tm.Steps) > 1 {
132			mean = cached / time.Duration(len(tm.Steps)-1)
133		}
134		fmt.Printf("%dx%d in %v: encode %v (%d tokens), prefill %v, %d cached steps mean %v, decode %v\n",
135			tm.Width, tm.Height, tm.Total.Round(time.Millisecond),
136			tm.Encode.Round(time.Millisecond), tm.Tokens,
137			tm.Prefill.Round(time.Millisecond), len(tm.Steps)-1, mean.Round(time.Millisecond),
138			tm.Decode.Round(time.Millisecond))
139	}
140	
141	func writePNG(path string, img *zvae.Tensor, opaque bool) error {
142		f, err := os.Create(path)
143		if err != nil {
144			return err
145		}
146		defer f.Close()
147		return png.Encode(f, pipeline.ToImage(img, opaque))
148	}
149	
150	func must(err error) {
151		if err != nil {
152			log.Fatal(err)
153		}
154	}

+// has to be a device test because what is under test is *when* the run stops
+// rather than that it eventually errors.
+// Three things are asserted, and the third is the one that would hurt:
+//   - the sampler stops at the step boundary, so a cancel two steps into
+//     eight costs about two steps and not eight;
+//   - the decoder stops between submit batches, so a cancel during the VAE
+//     costs a fraction of the decode rather than all of it;
+//   - **the pipeline still works afterwards**. A cancelled run leaves a
+//     recorded graph half-submitted and the arenas holding an abandoned
+//     image, so the next request is the real question, and it is answered by
+//     running one and comparing it against the same image generated without
+//     any cancellation in front of it. Bit-identical, not merely plausible.
+// The error identity matters as much as the timing: `errors.Is(err,
+// context.Canceled)` is what api.backendError keys on to answer with nothing
+// instead of a 500, so it is asserted rather than assumed.
+func TestCancellation(t *testing.T) {
+  if testing.Short() {
+    t.Skip("stages the whole pipeline")
+  dev, done := newTestDevice(t)
+  t.Cleanup(done)
+  const (
+    side  = 512
+    steps = 8
+  p := newPipeline(t, dev, Options{Model: model, Width: side, Height: side, Steps: steps})
+  // The uncancelled run first: it is both the reference image and the wall
+  // clock everything below is read against.
+  full := time.Now()
+  want, tm, err := p.Run(t.Context(), Request{
+    Prompt: defaultSweepPrompt, Width: side, Height: side, Steps: steps, Seed: 42,
+  if err != nil {
+    t.Fatal(err)
+  baseline := time.Since(full)
+  t.Logf("uncancelled: %v total (%d steps, decode %v)",
+    baseline.Round(time.Millisecond), len(tm.Steps), tm.Decode.Round(time.Millisecond))
+  // ---- Cancelled two steps in.
+  t.Run("sampler", func(t *testing.T) {
+    ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(t.Context())
+    defer cancel()
+    var reached int
+    start := time.Now()
+    _, _, err := p.Run(ctx, Request{
+      Prompt: defaultSweepPrompt, Width: side, Height: side, Steps: steps, Seed: 42,
+      Progress: func(st Step) {
+        reached = st.Index
+        if st.Index == 1 {
+          cancel()
+    elapsed := time.Since(start)
+    if !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
+      t.Fatalf("err %v, want context.Canceled", err)
+    // Two steps ran and the third was refused, so the run cost about a
+    // quarter of the schedule. Half the baseline is a loose bound that a
+    // run-to-completion cannot pass.
+    if elapsed > baseline/2 {
+      t.Errorf("cancelled at step 1 of %d but took %v of a %v run",
+        steps, elapsed.Round(time.Millisecond), baseline.Round(time.Millisecond))
+    t.Logf("cancelled after step %d: %v (%.0f%% of the full run): %v",
+      reached, elapsed.Round(time.Millisecond), 100*float64(elapsed)/float64(baseline), err)
+  // ---- Cancelled inside the VAE, which is one call and 30 submits.
+  t.Run("decoder", func(t *testing.T) {
+    latents := p.noise(geom{latentH: side / VAEScale, latentW: side / VAEScale,
+      imgTokens: (side / VAEScale) * (side / VAEScale)}, 7)
+    clean := time.Now()

+    time.AfterFunc(decode/8, cancel)
+    start := time.Now()

content.content:
So the framing is free and three in-progress frames cost **0.3%** — against
4.4% through taef1 — and what they buy is a picture at 2.3 seconds instead
of at ten. The frames land at 2.27, 4.34 and 6.43 s, from steps 3, 7 and 11
of the sixteen.

A preview decode itself is **159 µs** against a 587 ms step; everything else
in that 0.3% is encoding the PNG and writing it. Partial frames go out at
`png.BestSpeed` — 15% more bytes for a fifth of the latency — while the
finished image keeps the careful encoder. A transient frame and a deliverable
are not the same object. **A frame is 1/16 scale** (32x32 for a 512x512
image, 64x64 for a 1024x1024 one) and is upscaled by whatever displays it: a
latent2rgb map carries composition, colour and layout, and cannot carry
texture the latent does not hold per-pixel.

**What the frame decodes is the denoised estimate, not the current latent**,
and the distinction is load-bearing. The schedule is flow matching, so the
sample at step k is an interpolation x_t = (1−σ)·x0 + σ·ε — ten steps into
forty it is still three quarters noise, and mapping *that* through any
decoder gives a picture of noise. The estimate x0 = x_t − σ·v is what looks
like the image, and the loop forms it for nothing because it has the
velocity in hand.

**Which steps a partial comes from is the backend's decision**, not the
handler's: the step count may not have been named in the request, and how
finished a picture looks at step k is the scheduler's business. `backend`
spreads them evenly over the steps that will actually run and never takes the
last, whose denoised estimate *is* the final latent — a frame there would be
the finished image sent twice, once through each decoder.

**A client that hangs up stops the run**, streamed or not. A denoising step

arithmetic it saves: one lock serialises every model in the process, so an
abandoned image used to hold the queued speech, transcription and embedding
requests behind it for its full duration. Text completions have always
cancelled this way, between tokens; images, speech and transcription checked
only on the way in, and images now check throughout.

  fixing.** A denoising step *is* a submit-and-fence with nothing to abandon
  inside it — that much was true and is why no kernel changed here — but
  between two steps nothing is in flight, and the VAE already batches its
  dispatches four at a time for the driver's watchdog, which is 30 more
  boundaries in a 1024² decode. So the finest available granularity was never
  "the whole image"; it was one step and one batch, and nobody had gone and
  taken it.

  boundary safe in the first place.

  for every vertical in the process (one queue, nothing in `vk` externally
  synchronised), and it is held for the whole run — so an abandoned image
  was holding every queued speech, transcription and embedding request
  behind it for its full duration, not merely wasting its own GPU time.

  transcription still check only on the way in**, and are the same shape of
  fix if an utterance ever gets long enough to care.
  One thing came free with it: `cmd/qimage` takes its context from
  `signal.NotifyContext`, so Ctrl-C now unwinds a run through the same path a
  hung-up client takes rather than killing the process mid-submit.

Done and measured.

## What changed

The context now reaches every long-running stage instead of stopping at `backend.Image.Generate`'s front door:

- **`denoise`** checks between steps (`qimage/pipeline/gpu.go`) — the one place where nothing is in flight.
- **`engine.runContext`** in `qimage/vae` checks between submit batches. The batching already existed (4 dispatches per submit, a driver-watchdog constraint), so a 1024² decode has 30 boundaries for free.
- **The vision tower's `run`** does the same at 8 per submit, and `Encode`/`Forward`/`Decode` all take a `ctx` — so an edit's tower (6.3 s) and VAE encode (1.7 s) are interruptible too, plus a check between reference images, where the Lanczos resize is host work with no dispatch boundary of its own.
- `backend/image.go` passes `r.Context()` into both entry points.

## The gate

`TestCancellation` at 512²/8, where a full run is 6.27 s:

```
uncancelled:  6.265s total (8 steps, decode 1.663s)
sampler:      cancelled after step 1 → 1.301s (21% of the full run)
              "pipeline: cancelled at step 2 of 8: context canceled"
decoder:      cancelled ⅛ into a 1.707s decode → 295ms,
              "qvae: cancelled after 12 of 117 dispatches: context canceled"
```

At the served 1024²/40 shape that's ~2.2 s of a 92 s image instead of 92.

The third assertion is the one that mattered most: a cancelled run leaves a recorded graph half-submitted and the arenas holding an abandoned image, so the test runs a **fourth generation after both cancellations and requires it bit-identical** to the one before them. It is — nothing is left in flight to survive a cancel, which is the same property that makes the step boundary safe.

Errors wrap `ctx.Err()`, so `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` still holds at `api.backendError` and a hangup stays "no answer" rather than becoming a 500.

## Checks

`TestServedEditOracle256` re-run to cover the edit path (I renamed a local `ctx` that shadowed the new parameter): **max abs 0.0014, mean 1.7e-4** — the same digits IMAGE.md records, and the blank-reference control still fires at 366x. Full short suite, vet and gofmt clean.

One free extra: `cmd/qimage` takes its context from `signal.NotifyContext`, so Ctrl-C unwinds a run through the same path rather than killing the process mid-submit.

Documented as Q11 in `IMAGE.md`, with the API.md paragraph that described the old bargain rewritten.

Two things I did **not** change, both flagged in the docs rather than silently left: **TTS and STT still check only on entry** — same shape of fix, and worth doing if an utterance ever gets long enough to care — and the DiT step itself is still atomic, which is the 2.2 s floor on how fast an image can stop. The offer from before also still stands: the running `ai` service has neither this nor the geometry fix until it's rebuilt and restarted.
